reason: The cited evidence supports that laser-clad HEAs can produce hard, wear-resistant coatings on steels, but neither passage addresses hot-cracking mitigation, HAZ reduction, or repair of crack-prone components, which are central premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a metallurgically bonded HEA overlay with low dilution and fast solidification.
HEA coatings (e.g., FeCrNiTiZr, AlCoCrFeNi) can provide high hardness and elevated-temperature wear resistance on steel substrates.
The rapid solidification and controlled heat input of laser cladding minimize the HAZ and avoid brittle interdendritic phases that cause hot cracking.
A laser-clad HEA overlay can serve as an effective repair material for hot-working tool steels.
